title: The Sweet Songbook
premise: Freya Kavanagh has spent ten years exchanging anonymous letters with 'A.'—a pen pal who kept her afloat after her daughter's father left—never knowing he was Theo Marchetti, the sommelier-turned-vineyard-manager whose family estate once tried to buy out her bookshop block. When Theo moves in next door to oversee the vineyard's first harvest under his own name, they recognize each other's handwriting within weeks, and a friendship that was safe on paper becomes dangerous in person. As developers circle the bookshop and Theo's family demands he return to the city career that rescued him from ruin, both must decide whether love is something you contain or something you survive. The novel ends at the first harvest festival, where Freya signs papers to keep the shop through a co-op of townspeople, and Theo chooses her—mailing one last letter to her own address, signed with his real name.
about_author: W. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who now writes love stories set in places where everyone knows your overdue fines. Sterling lives near a working vineyard and insists the best romances ripen slowly, like late-season grapes.

chapters.title: Return to Sender
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Opening on the tenth anniversary of the letters, Freya rereads the first one while closing up the Sweet Songbook, establishing her rule that the heart is trainable. Her daughter Poppy asks who 'A.' is; Freya deflects. Emotional beat: tender loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives at the cottage next to the bookshop, sent by his family to manage the vineyard's make-or-break first harvest. He recognizes Freya's handwriting on a returned parcel addressed in the same slanted script as ten years of letters—and says nothing. Emotional beat: guilty longing and fear of exposure.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Freya and Theo collide over borrowed books left on each other's porches, their marginal notes echoing phrases from the letters. Neither admits what they suspect; both test it. Emotional beat: flirtation sharpened by secrecy, the thrill of being half-seen.

chapters.title: What the Vineyard Owes
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A video call with Theo's brother reveals the family expects him back in the city wine trade by winter—the career that rebuilt him after bankruptcy. He learns the vineyard's investors also hold the loan on Freya's building. Emotional beat: dread as duty tightens its grip.

chapters.title: Rain on the Reading Room
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A storm floods the bookshop's back room; Theo shows up unasked and works beside her until midnight. Poppy falls asleep on his shoulder. Freya feels the containment she trained into herself beginning to fail. Emotional beat: warmth breaking through armor.

chapters.title: The Handwriting on the Wall
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Poppy finds an old letter in Theo's cottage and matches it to the shop's archive box. Confronted gently, Theo confesses he is 'A.' Freya's relief curdles when she realizes he knew for months and stayed silent. Emotional beat: intimacy achieved and immediately wounded.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya withdraws; Theo throws himself into harvest prep. The developer's offer on the bookshop block goes formal, backed by the vineyard investors, forcing Theo to choose sides publicly or lose everything he built. Emotional beat: isolation, the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the eve of harvest, Theo writes the confession he owes: why he hid, what the letters meant, what he's willing to lose. His brother arrives demanding he sign the buyout and come home. Emotional beat: quiet resolve crystallizing into choice.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the harvest festival, Freya prepares to sign the sale papers alone until townspeople arrive with a co-op counteroffer Theo secretly organized, risking his inheritance. She reads his unsent letter, delivered by Poppy. Emotional beat: found family rallying; the heart refusing containment.

chapters.title: Signed, With My Real Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV converging on Freya's. Amid the crush of the first pressing, Freya and Theo finally speak plainly—about the decade of letters, the silence, the fear. He stays through the harvest; she keeps the shop. The last scene mirrors the first: a new letter, hand-delivered, no longer anonymous. Emotional beat: love chosen over safety, fully seen at last.
